channel.title: EVOLVE Journal
channel.description: Researched guides to getting outside in Canada, from EVOLVE Apparel.

item.title: The Most Romantic Winter Getaways in Alberta
item.description: Romantic getaways Alberta winter: glass cabins, domes, lake lodges and private wood-fired tubs you can drive to. Rates checked late November 2026.

item.title: Banff in December: Christmas in the Rockies
item.description: Banff in December means short cold days, a Christmas market to December 13, 2026, Lake Louise skating, and priced Christmas dinners in town.

item.title: Where the Signal Dies: Off-Grid Backcountry Lodges and Huts You Can Ski or Snowshoe Into
item.description: Backcountry lodges in BC and huts in Alberta you ski or snowshoe into this winter: 2026 to 2027 prices, access, permits, and avalanche rules.

item.title: The Powder Highway: A Road Trip Through BC's Deepest Snow
item.description: Powder Highway BC for 2026 to 2027: eight Kootenay resorts, posted opening dates, pass rules, Rogers Pass, and the drive from Calgary or Edmonton.

item.title: Minus Thirty and Wide Open: Western Canada's Best Winter Adventures
item.description: Western Canada's best winter adventures for 2026-27: ten festivals, icewalks, and skating trails across BC, the Prairies, and the North, in date order.

item.title: First Hole: A Beginner's Field Guide to Ice Fishing in Alberta
item.description: Ice fishing in Alberta for beginners: licence costs, safe ice thickness, the rules, stocked trout ponds near Edmonton and Calgary, gear and what to wear.

item.title: First Snow, Best Views: 10 Places in Western Canada That Get Better When the Snow Falls
item.description: The best places to visit in Western Canada in winter: Lake Louise, Abraham Lake's ice bubbles, frozen canyons, the Icefields Parkway, Tofino storms and more.

item.title: Bear Country Manners: What to Actually Do When You Meet a Grizzly
item.description: What to do if you meet a grizzly or black bear in Canada: ID tips, bear spray, bluff charges, food caches, dogs and bikes — Parks Canada–sourced for Alberta & BC trails.

item.title: The 10 Best Places to Stay in Western Canada With a Breathtaking View From Your Room
item.description: The 10 best places to stay in Western Canada with a view from your room: Rockies lakes, Pacific storms and aurora, with prices and how to get there.

item.title: The Long Haul: Canada's Greatest Road Trips, With the Gas Stations Nobody Warns You About
item.description: Six iconic Canadian road trips—Icefields Parkway, Alaska Highway, Stewart-Cassiar, Dempster, Cowboy Trail, and Trans-Labrador—plus every fuel gap.

item.title: Chasing Green: Where to See the Northern Lights in Alberta and Western Canada
item.description: Where to see the northern lights in Alberta and Western Canada: KP index and aurora forecasts, best months, dark-sky parks, camera settings and cold tips.

item.title: Hot Water, Cold Air: Western Canada's Best Natural Hot Springs, Ranked
item.description: The best hot springs in Western Canada, ranked from the Alaska Highway to Kootenay Lake, with fees, seasons and rules before you soak.

item.title: No Mountains Required: The Best Hikes Within Two Hours of Edmonton
item.description: The best hikes near Edmonton: river valley, parkland and boreal trails close to the city, plus Elk Island and day trips within two hours.

item.title: Deep Wild, Good Sheets: Five Canadian Nature Resorts Worth the Drive or the Floatplane
item.description: The best nature resorts in Canada: wilderness lodges with full comfort, from a fly-in BC archipelago to a Quebec lake in moose country.

item.title: Stand Here: The Ten Most Breathtaking Views in Canada and How to Reach Them
item.description: The 10 most breathtaking views in Canada and how to reach them, from Moraine Lake in Banff to Virginia Falls, twice the height of Niagara.

item.title: Cold and Free: Five Canadian Adventure Sports Worth the Adrenaline
item.description: Canadian adventure sports the world copies, from heli-skiing where it was invented to year-round Pacific surfing, and how beginners can start.

item.title: Descended from Survivors: Ten Backcountry Skills the First Canadians Knew and We Forgot
item.description: Survival skills of Canada's first peoples: how Indigenous knowledge made life at minus forty possible, and how settlers survived by learning it.

item.title: Learning to Climb in Canada: Where to Start Mountaineering Without Getting in Over Your Head
item.description: How to learn mountaineering in Canada: courses, guides and the right order to go from your first scramble to a glaciated summit.

item.title: Pack Light, Eat Smart: The Beginner's Hike-Packing Kit People Always Get Wrong
item.description: A lightweight hiking packing list: the Ten Essentials, trail food math and the small items people forget, for day hikes and multi-day trips.

item.title: Build Your Own Off-Grid Escape: Cheap Land, Solar, and a Wood-Fired Soak Near Canada's Best Parks
item.description: How to build an off-grid cabin in Canada: affordable land near great parks, the permit rules nobody warns you about, and the off-grid tech.

item.title: Vancouver Island, End to End: Ten Places Worth the Ferry
item.description: The best places on Vancouver Island beyond Tofino, from old-growth giants and Victoria to an orca strait and the wild north tip.

item.title: The Best Hikes in Alberta and BC: 8 Day Trips and Two Big Ones Worth the Sweat
item.description: The best hikes in Alberta and BC, with real distances, elevation gain and permit rules for standout day hikes and bigger summer trips.

item.title: The 10 Best National Parks in Canada, Ranked by Someone Who Has Opinions
item.description: The 10 best national parks in Canada, ranked, with the one thing worth going for in each park and a practical tip for your visit.

item.title: The Best Ski Resorts in Alberta: A Rider's Field Guide to the Big Three
item.description: The best ski resorts in Alberta: how to ski and ride Sunshine Village, Lake Louise and Marmot Basin, with terrain tips for each mountain.

item.title: Ten Boutique Cabins and Lodges in Canada Worth the Drive (or the Floatplane)
item.description: Ten boutique cabins and lodges in Canada, from a hanging sphere on Vancouver Island to a glass-roofed aurora chalet in the Yukon.
